title: Surgical capacity drain and tenant fairness playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
During the hosted API GPU exhaustion event on 2026-02-27 we observed protracted cross-tenant queue buildup that degraded p95/p99 latency for healthy tenants. Existing bulk-shed policies were too coarse: whole-pool throttles triggered, causing overkill degradation for low-risk tenants while noisy workloads continued to amplify KV cache pressure and prefetch storms. This ticket captures a surgical, automatable playbook to drain backlog selectively, reestablish fair share, and close key telemetry gaps so we can detect and act earlier next time.

Goals:
- Stop latency amplification for unaffected tenants within 3 minutes of playbook activation.
- Reduce GPU-backed queue length by 70% within 20 minutes using targeted admission and soft-drain operations.
- Restore fair throughput distribution across high/low-risk tenants without full-pool-wide drops.
- Automate most remediation steps to run in an operator-approved workflow with one-click escalation.

Root causes observed:
- Tenant-local KV-cache pollution caused long KV miss tails, increasing per-request GPU time and reducing throughput.
- Noisy tenants submitted many short, high-concurrency requests that prevented prewarm from amortizing cost.
- Coarse admission gates only supported pool-level throttles; lack of tenant-level surgical ejection meant collateral damage.
- Telemetry for tenant-level KV hit-rate and per-tenant running-KV-size was noisy/missing, delaying diagnosis by ~7 minutes.

Planned deliverables (MVP):
1) Surgical Drain Command (operator tooling) - a runbook action that:
   - takes a tenant or shard id and marks it for staged soft-drain (new tenant-level admission multiplier + immediate prefetch-stop).
   - reduces concurrent slots for the tenant (configurable ratio) and enqueues a graceful queue-drain sequence that rejects new prefetches but finishes in-flight requests up to a short time budget.
   - optional ephemeral eviction of large KV-entries for the tenant via a safe compaction heuristic.
2) Tenant Fairness Scorer & Admission Multiplier - lightweight scoring function combining: running-concurrency, recent error-rate, KV-hit-rate, and estimated GPU-time-per-request. Multiplier applied before pool admission decisions.
3) KV-telemetry improvements - instrument per-tenant KV hit/miss counts, top-n keys by size, and 95th-percentile cache-residency. Surface flagged tenants in Console Incident view.
4) Automated escalation workflow - a one-click console action that runs the surgical drain sequence and opens a coordination thread with stakeholders while attaching suggested tenants to evict.
5) Acceptance tests & chaos scenarios - synthetic tenant noise generator to validate that surgical drain reduces collateral impact vs pool-wide throttles.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 0 (this ticket): finalize playbook steps, definitions for "surgical drain" and admission multiplier; design API for operator tool.
- Week 1: implement scoring function and admission multiplier in the admission service (feature-flagged). Add unit tests.
- Week 2: implement surgical drain control path + safe KV compaction hooks (runtime changes minimal, opt-in via admin flags).
- Week 3: wire KV telemetry and Console incident UI flag. Build one-click escalation UI.
- Week 4: run chaos tests in staging and measure p95/p99 regressions. Iterate.

Safety and rollback:
- All surgical-drain controls must be behind admin permission and an explicit feature flag per pool.
- Surgical drains operate in staged levels (observe-only -> soft-drain -> hard-eject) with timed automatic rollback.
- Admission multiplier default bounds: [0.2, 1.0] to avoid immediate full ejects.

Acceptance criteria (AC):
- AC1: Activating surgical drain on staging reduces p99 latency for baseline tenants by >=60% within 15 minutes compared to baseline without surgical drain.
- AC2: Admission multiplier score computation is stable under 1000 tenants and adds <10% RPS overhead to admission path.
- AC3: Console shows per-tenant KV hit/miss metrics and flags top-5 noisy tenants during a synthetic storm.
- AC4: Oncall runbook reduced time-to-decision by 5+ minutes in tabletop exercises.

Out-of-scope for MVP:
- Global autoscaler policy rewrite.
- Long-term billing throttles or customer-visible quota changes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should the automatic compaction be? We prefer conservative defaults but need a plan for manual escalation when soft-drain isn't enough.
- Admission multiplier weighting: relative weight of KV-miss vs concurrency needs calibration with 2 controlled experiments.

- Staging chaos harness: https://ci.redwood.ai/chaos/tenant-noise-generator/exp-14

Next steps (short term):
- [ ] Finalize scoring function and expose toggle in admission service (owner: Marco Chen).
- [ ] Add minimal KV instrumentation (owner: Priya Gupta) and pipeline to Console incident view (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- [ ] Implement operator surgical-drain command-line endpoint and Console button (owner: Marco Chen).
- [ ] Write staging test scenarios and run two controlled experiments comparing surgical drain vs pool-wide throttle (owner: SRE team).
